curriculum.lesson_evidence: Singing is easier and safer for your voice when you warm up first with gentle sounds. Try a siren, sliding your voice from low to high and back with an 'oo' sound, and humming. To match pitch, listen first to the note, think of it in your head and then sing it back. Sing at a comfortable volume, stand tall with relaxed shoulders and sip water. Never shout or strain, and stop if your throat feels sore. If you are not comfortable singing, you can hum or tap the pitch pattern.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Your partner sings 'low, high, high' and you need to match it. Write what you will do before singing, and how you will fix it if your note is wrong.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: 'I will listen to all three notes first, think them in my head, then sing low, high, high. If my high note is too low, I will listen again and slide my voice up a little.' Listening before singing and adjusting is how pitch matching works.

WATCH FOR
Thinking that you must sing loudly or high to be good at singing. Good singing is gentle, in tune and in time, and shouting can hurt your voice.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Play a pitch echo game with someone at home with five short patterns using high, middle and low notes. Write each pattern as H, M or L. Then do a siren warm-up and describe how your voice moved. Stop if your voice feels strained.

Write a short reflection naming one artistic choice you changed and why. Movement or instrument work is optional, adult-supervised and can be described instead.

teaching.why: This helps the learner make intentional visual, music, drama or dance choices and name their effect, rather than saying an artwork is simply “nice”. Keep every claim linked to an element or technique.
